Our objective: maximize distinct completed tasks (i.e., number of distinct tasks among the four agents). Then among those, minimize total execution cost across all four agents (the "total cost" column). Then tie-break lexicographically smallest (A-task, B-task). Both A and B share this objective, and they choose simultaneously without seeing each other's choice. So they must each choose a task that is consistent with equilibrium under common objective and tie-breaking.

We need to find the set of (A,B) pairs that are optimal according to the criteria, given that both agents will choose simultaneously. Since they have identical preferences and tie-breaking rule, they will aim to select the lexicographically smallest (A,B) among optimal outcomes. However, they cannot coordinate, but they both know the rule; they both will choose the same (A,B) pair? Actually they need to choose tasks individually; they cannot both choose two tasks simultaneously? They choose simultaneously, each picks a task. The equilibrium is that both will pick the tasks from the lexicographically smallest optimal pair. Since they have same objective and tie-breaking, they will both pick the same tasks as indicated by that pair. That yields that A picks the A-task from that pair.
